title: Site Design Configuration
description: Visual design configuration for colors, typography, layout, and effects

primary.description: The dominant brand color used throughout the site. Based on the site's theme and content categories, choose a color that reinforces the intended mood and purpose. For example: professional/technical sites may use blue or green; creative/artistic sites may use purple, orange, or unconventional hues; nature/outdoor sites may use greens or earth tones; finance sites may use blue or green. Consider color psychology and ensure sufficient contrast against the background for accessibility.

secondary.description: Interaction color — used for hovers, focus states, and active transitions. Should be visually distinct from primary but harmonious (e.g. a darker/lighter shade, complementary hue, or analogous color). Default: #64748b.

background.description: The base background color for the entire site, including the main content area and page backgrounds. Choose based on the overall mood: light backgrounds (e.g., #f8fafc, #ffffff) create a clean, professional, or airy feel suitable for most content-heavy sites; dark backgrounds (e.g., #0f172a, #1e293b) convey modernity, sophistication, or focus, ideal for media, portfolios, or dark-mode-first sites; neutral mid-tones (e.g., #e2e8f0, #cbd5e1) offer a balanced, soft alternative. Ensure sufficient contrast with the text color for accessibility.

surface.description: The surface color used for cards, modals, dropdowns, and other elevated UI elements. Should be visually distinct from the background but harmonious — typically a slightly lighter or darker shade, or a subtle complementary tone. For light backgrounds, use a slightly off-white (e.g., #f1f5f9, #f8fafc); for dark backgrounds, use a slightly lighter dark tone (e.g., #1e293b, #334155). This creates depth and hierarchy without overwhelming the primary color.

text.description: The primary text color for headings, body text, and prominent labels. Should provide sufficient contrast against the background color for readability (WCAG AA standard: 4.5:1 ratio recommended). For light backgrounds, use dark grays or near-black (e.g., #1e293b, #334155, #0f172a) rather than pure black for a softer look; for dark backgrounds, use light grays or off-white (e.g., #e2e8f0, #f1f5f9, #f8fafc). Avoid pure black (#000000) and pure white (#ffffff) as they can cause eye strain and harsh contrast.

text_muted.description: The secondary text color for metadata, captions, secondary labels, timestamps, and less important text. Should be lighter than the primary text color but still readable (WCAG AA standard: 3:1 ratio recommended). For light backgrounds, use medium grays (e.g., #64748b, #475569, #334155); for dark backgrounds, use medium-light grays (e.g., #94a3b8, #cbd5e1, #e2e8f0). Avoid colors that are too close to the background or too close to the primary text color, which would create visual confusion.

accent.description: The highlight color used for key interactive elements — buttons, active states, notifications, and primary call-to-actions. Should be visually distinct from primary and background, ideally a complementary or analogous hue that draws attention without overwhelming the primary brand color. Unlike the secondary color which handles subtle interaction states (hovers, focus), accent is reserved for prominent, eye-catching elements that need to stand out. For example: if primary is blue (#2563eb), accent might be orange (#f97316) or teal (#14b8a6) to create dynamic contrast; if primary is purple (#7c3aed), accent could be yellow (#eab308) or pink (#ec4899). Use sparingly to guide user focus and enhance visual hierarchy.

error.description: Color for error states (e.g., 404 pages, failed image placeholders)

success.description: Color for success states (e.g., confirmation messages, form completions)

dark.description: Optional dark mode color palette. All fields are optional; omitting any field applies its default or uses the light mode value.

font_family.description: Primary font for body text. Choose a font matching your site's mood (e.g., Inter for professional, Merriweather for editorial). This is a CSS font-family stack — include fallbacks like 'Inter, system-ui, sans-serif'. System fonts are automatic fallbacks. You have access to Google Fonts: browse at https://fonts.google.com

font_size_base.description: Base font size for body text and standard paragraphs (e.g., '16px', '1rem'). Choose a size that ensures readability while matching your site's scale. Common values: '16px' (standard), '18px' (generous), '14px' (compact). Pair with your chosen font's x-height for optimal readability.

heading_font.description: Font family for all headings (h1-h6, titles, labels). Choose a font that complements your body font and matches your site's tone (e.g., Playfair Display for elegant, Oswald for bold, Roboto for neutral). This is a CSS font-family stack — include fallbacks. You have access to Google Fonts: browse at https://fonts.google.com

heading_size_scale.description: Optical size correction factor for the heading font. Fonts with a small x-height (e.g. Playfair Display, Cormorant Garamond) typically need 1.1–1.15. Fonts with a large x-height (e.g. Oswald, Raleway) may need 0.9–0.95.

sidebar_width.description: Width of the sidebar (e.g., '280px', '300px', '320px'). Choose a width that balances navigation visibility with content space. Narrower (280px) is compact for dense content; wider (300-320px) is spacious for feature-rich sites.

max_width.description: Maximum content width for the main area (e.g., '1200px', '1400px', '1600px'). Choose based on content density: narrower (1200px) for text-heavy sites; wider (1400-1600px) for image/media-heavy sites.

effects.description: Visual personality of the site. All fields are optional; omitting any field applies its default. Combine these to produce distinct styles — see description of each value for guidance.

card_style.description: Dominant visual treatment of link cards. 'image-overlay': dark gradient over thumbnail image, white text — cinematic, editorial, media/inspiration boards. 'flat': solid surface background, no shadow, dark text — clean, academic, documentation, professional directories. 'outlined': bold primary-color border, no shadow, dark text — editorial, developer tools, zines, technical references. 'elevated': strong drop shadow, no border, dark text — product directories, SaaS tools, dashboards.

shadow_intensity.description: Global shadow depth applied to cards, modals, and dropdowns. 'none': completely flat, zero elevation — brutalist, ultra-minimal, print-inspired. 'subtle': barely perceptible lift — light and clean, suits most sites. 'medium': clear depth — professional, balanced. 'dramatic': strong, deep shadows — rich and bold, pairs well with 'elevated' card_style.

border_radius.description: Corner rounding applied globally to cards, buttons, inputs, modals, tags, and badges. 'sharp': 0px — structured, technical, brutalist, newspaper-style. 'standard': 8px — neutral and professional, suits most domains. 'soft': 16px — friendly, approachable, modern consumer feel. 'round': 24px — playful, lifestyle, children's content, social platforms.

border_treatment.description: Style of structural dividers: sidebar border, header underline, footer top border, and card borders in non-overlay card styles. 'none': no visible borders, separation by spacing and shadow only — airy and modern. 'hairline': barely visible 1px lines — clean neutral default. 'bold': 2px dark borders — assertive, editorial, high-contrast. 'accent': 2px borders using the primary color — strongly branded, high visual identity.

hover_effect.description: Animation feedback when hovering over link cards. 'none': no animation — static, document-like, suitable for accessibility-first or print-inspired designs. 'lift': card rises slightly with translateY — default tactile feel. 'glow': colored halo using the primary color — vivid, creative, gaming, entertainment. 'outline': crisp border appears on hover — sharp and keyboard-navigation-friendly, suits technical and developer-focused sites.

heading_style.description: Typographic personality of all headings and prominent labels (site title, card titles, intro title, modal title). 'natural': standard weight and spacing — neutral and versatile, good default. 'editorial': tight negative letter-spacing, heavy weight — bold, modern, journalistic. 'elegant': wide letter-spacing, light weight — refined, cultural institutions, high-end collections, art. 'uppercase': all-caps with tracked spacing, strong weight — structured, institutional, signage-like, technical directories.
